title: Mrs. Michal Tawil: Personal and National Torah (Class # 15)

chapters.title: Yom Hazikaron and Yom Ha'atzmaut
chapters.about: Reflections on Memorial Day in Israel and the sacrifice of soldiers.

chapters.title: The Role of a Parent
chapters.about: Learning to support children without becoming consumed by their choices.

chapters.title: The Personal Torah of Parents
chapters.about: Stories of Michal Peretz and others finding deeper messages from parents.

chapters.title: Har Sinai and Collective Mission
chapters.about: How the Torah creates unity and removes loneliness.

claims: "She also reflects on the significance of Yom Hazikaron and the collective mission of the Jewish people." - The transcript does not contain a reflection on the collective mission of the Jewish people in the context of Yom Hazikaron; the teacher discusses the collective mission in the context of Har Sinai and the Jewish people as a nation.

"She explains that by looking past the superficial actions of our family members to find the deeper values they are teaching, we can better understand our mission and connect to Hashem." - The teacher specifically discusses uncovering the 'personal Torah' of parents and spouses, not 'family members' in general.
summary: Mrs. Tawil discusses the importance of introspection and uncovering the personal Torah passed down through our parents and spouses. She explains that by looking past the superficial actions of our family members to find the deeper values they are teaching, we can better understand our mission and connect to Hashem. She also reflects on the significance of Yom Hazikaron and the collective mission of the Jewish people.
questions: How can we find the deeper meaning behind our parents' or spouses' actions?
What is the significance of Yom Hazikaron for the Jewish people?
How does uncovering our personal family Torah help us connect to Hashem?
Why is it important to move beyond superficial arguments with family members?
How can we overcome feelings of loneliness by focusing on a shared mission?
